entities.summary: Thomas Shepard was an English, afterwards American Puritan minister and a significant figure in early colonial New England. He was born in 1605, in Nottinghamshire, England, and studied at Emmanuel College, Cambridge. Shepard was ordained as a minister in 1627 and served in the Church of England until 1637, when he was dispossessed and forced to flee to Massachusetts Bay Colony. There, he played a key role in the establishment of the first Baptist church in the American colonies and became a prominent figure in the Puritan community. Shepard married Mary Rowlandson, a survivor of the 1675 Indian massacre, and they had four children together. He died on August 25, 1649, in Newbury, Massachusetts, and his legacy as a pioneering American Baptist continues to be felt in the United States. Shepard's writings, including his influential book 'The Body of Divinity,' remain widely read and studied by scholars and theologians today.
